video_title: Tim Legler reveals how De’Aaron Fox can bounce back from Game 4 woes 👀 | The Rich Eisen Show

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: De'Aaron Fox's decision-making on final play against the Pistons
quotes.excerpt: The play was to veer off, take the foul, eat clock, and put your team up three.
quotes.quote: The decision-making in that situation is you veer off, you kill a couple more seconds, they are going to grab you. You are going to get fouled, but you probably ate up another two seconds there. And then you have to go to the line and make two very big, important, pressure free throws, which the guy has been an excellent free-throw shooter throughout his career. That is the play to make. I think he was just counting on his speed. He is one of the quickest guys in the league and he thought he could get his hands on that basketball and beat whoever was trailing him to the rim.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' historic shooting performance in the first half
quotes.excerpt: They hit 14 threes in the first half. It was a historic shooting performance by Finals standards.
quotes.quote: They hit 14 threes in the first half. It was a historic shooting performance by Finals standards. They have this big lead. They come out to start the third quarter, you are still dipping your toe in that water. They were getting whatever they wanted, they were in great flow, and they continued to take those shots.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' math problem regarding deficit and time
quotes.excerpt: The only way you can solve this math problem in terms of the deficit is quick shots.
quotes.quote: I keep referring to this as a math problem for the Knicks. The only way you can solve this math problem in terms of the deficit and the time on the clock is you are going to need help. And how do you get that help? There is two ways: quick shots by the Spurs that do not go in and turnovers, because you need more possessions and you need more time.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.excerpt: I didn't like that first bump call right off the bat on Karl-Anthony Towns.
quotes.quote: There were some calls clearly in that game that you felt like were 50-50 type situations. I didn't like that first bump call right off the bat on Karl-Anthony Towns on that drive by De'Aaron Fox. That is the first possession. Fox turns the corner on him and he is fairly vertical and it is just a bump where he catches him a little bit.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: How foul trouble impacts a big man's aggressiveness
quotes.excerpt: It affects your aggressiveness driving to the rim. You don't want to pick up a charge.
quotes.quote: It affects your aggressiveness driving to the rim. You don't want to pick up a charge. It affects your aggressiveness as a screener, and that is a big part of Karl-Anthony Towns' game. And now you are just tiptoeing around on eggshells a little bit and it just affects your aggressiveness.
